profile.reading:
This is Digital Realty facility SJC10, at 1100 Space Park Drive, Santa Clara, CA 95054. Digital Realty's own property listing for SJC10, fetched this session, lists the building at 163,500 square feet.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building sits within Digital Realty's Silicon Valley campus, a dense cluster of buildings across Santa Clara and Santa Clara County that is one of the company's oldest US footprints, reflecting the area's history as a birthplace of the commercial colocation and internet exchange industry. Digital Realty's own Silicon Valley metro page, fetched this session, lists numerous named properties concentrated along Comstock Street, Lafayette Street, and Walsh Avenue, ranging from under 15,000 to nearly 400,000 square feet each. The company does not publish a consolidated IT power rating in megawatts for individual Silicon Valley buildings in the sources reviewed this session.

Digital Realty markets its Silicon Valley properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Chicago, Dallas, and New York/New Jersey, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform. The company's FY2025 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage.

PG&E is the principal electric utility serving most of the area, and California's data center growth has drawn scrutiny over grid capacity and water use for cooling in recent years. reading.body:
Digital Realty SJC10 is a 163,500 square foot colocation building at 1100 Space Park Drive in Santa Clara, operated as a landlord facility rather than as a hyperscaler's own compute campus. The building's IT power capacity is not published by the operator on its property page or in its FY2025 10-K; without that figure, the scale of AI workload this specific building can host remains unknown. SJC10 is one of Digital Realty's individually coded properties within a dense cluster of dozens of smaller buildings across Santa Clara and Santa Clara County, many under 400,000 square feet each.

This facility ranks outside the top eleven published-capacity data centers in California, placing it among the majority of mapped sites that do not disclose megawatt ratings. Silicon Valley as a region hosts large campuses for Google, Meta, and numerous colocation tenants across PG&E territory, where grid capacity and cooling water availability have become design constraints in recent years. Digital Realty markets SJC10 under its PlatformDIGITAL colocation brand alongside Northern Virginia, Chicago, Dallas, and New York/New Jersey as core interconnection hubs.

Without a published power figure, SJC10 cannot be directly assessed for its contribution to AI scaling constraints. The absence of a disclosed rating from one of the largest colocation operators in the world suggests either that individual building figures are not material to Digital Realty's portfolio disclosure, or that the company prioritizes metro-level rather than building-level transparency. For a reader tracking grid-binding capacity, this facility's actual power draw and tenant composition would need to come from sources beyond the operator's public spec page.
